# Iterative convergence

A node should run again on its own output until some condition holds — refine, re-check, re-refine — and then hand the converged result downstream. Rimsky spells this as a **cycle in the subscription graph** with the stop condition written as a `when:` predicate on the back edge.

The predicate is what stops the loop. Any counter cap you also declare is a safety net, not the design.

## The shape

- The iterating node subscribes to its **own** `terminal/success` under a predicate that means "keep going".
- The downstream node subscribes to the same signal under the complementary predicate, "we are done".
- `cascade_mode: sequenced` on the iterating node keeps rounds from replacing each other.
- The whole iteration runs inside one frame.

## The template

```yaml
name: converge
version: "1"
description: One node iterates on its own output until the count reaches three, then hands off downstream.
nodes:
  - type: iterate
    kind: loop_counter
    cascade_mode: sequenced
    subscribes:
      - node: iterate
        type: terminal/success
        when: "payload.attributes_delta.count < 3"
        force_upstream_refresh: false
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          max:
            type: integer
            default: 50
          count:
            type: integer

  - type: downstream
    kind: attribute_passthrough
    subscribes:
      - node: iterate
        type: terminal/success
        when: "payload.attributes_delta.count >= 3"
        force_upstream_refresh: false
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          count:
            type: integer
            default: 0
```

Wake it with one empty message. `iterate` emits counts 1, 2, 3 and stops; `downstream` runs exactly once, on the converged output. The frame ends `completed` and the instance comes to rest with no live runs.

## The two-node form

A cycle does not have to be a self-loop. Two nodes pointing at each other iterate the same way:

```yaml
nodes:
  - type: seed
    kind: attribute_passthrough
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          count: { type: integer, default: 0 }

  - type: ping
    kind: loop_counter
    subscribes:
      - node: seed
        type: terminal/success
        force_upstream_refresh: false
      - node: pong
        type: terminal/success
        force_upstream_refresh: false
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          max: { type: integer, default: 50 }
          count: { type: integer }

  - type: pong
    kind: attribute_passthrough
    subscribes:
      - node: ping
        type: terminal/success
        when: "payload.attributes_delta.count < 3"
        force_upstream_refresh: false
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          count: { type: integer, default: 0 }

  - type: downstream
    kind: attribute_passthrough
    subscribes:
      - node: ping
        type: terminal/success
        when: "payload.attributes_delta.count >= 3"
        force_upstream_refresh: false
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          count: { type: integer, default: 0 }
```

`ping` emits 1, 2, 3; `pong` runs twice, once per round below the predicate; `downstream` runs once. That is also one frame.

## Writing the predicate

`when:` is a CEL expression that compiles at registration and evaluates during the cascade walk. Two variables bind: `type`, a string, and `payload`, a map.

| Signal | What `payload` carries |
| --- | --- |
| `terminal/success` | `changed`, `attributes_delta`, `change_summary`, `tags` |
| `terminal/error/<class>` | `error_class`, `error_payload`, `attempt`, `retries_so_far`, `attributes_delta`, `tags` |
| `attribute/<key>/changed` | `key`, `value`, `old_value` |

Read the value the sender just wrote with `payload.attributes_delta.<field>`. When `type:` is an exact path, field references are checked at registration and an unknown field fails; when `type:` ends in `*`, `payload` binds dynamically and no check runs. The CEL standard library is available and rimsky adds no helpers. A predicate that errors at evaluation is treated as no-match — which stops the loop silently, so keep predicates total.

## Two independent stops

The `loop_counter` kind carries its own cap in the `max` attribute. With `max: 4` it dispatches four times, tagging the rounds `loop`, `loop`, `loop`, `done`; with `max: 1` it dispatches once, tagged `done`. That cap and your predicate stop the loop for different reasons. Set the cap well above the rounds you expect so a real convergence failure surfaces as a runaway you notice, rather than as a silent truncation at the cap.

An alternative stop uses the tag instead of the count:

```yaml
      - node: iterate
        type: terminal/success
        when: '"loop" in payload.tags'
        force_upstream_refresh: false
```

## Sharp edges

**Subscribing is waking.** There is no declaration that reads a sender's data without also waking on it. Every `subscribes:` entry marks this node stale on a matching emission and gates its dispatch on the sender.

**`sequenced` keeps every round but not always their order.** No round is dropped. Where the receiver's own round is held and further rounds queue behind it, the rounds dispatch in arrival order. Where the sender instead **bursts** several rounds back to back inside one frame while the receiver is gated by the sender's in-flight run, every round still dispatches with its own inputs — nothing is coalesced — but the executor observes the **newest round first** and the earlier rounds after it: four, one, two, three at four rounds, and five, one, two, three, four at five. Do not build an accumulator, an audit trail, or rapid-flip detection on the assumption that a sequenced receiver sees rounds in the order they were sent.

**The other three cascade modes drop rounds by design.** `most-recent`, the default, deletes an unclaimed earlier round and keeps the newest. `idempotent-queue` drops a round whose resolved inputs are byte-identical to the most recent prior round. `idempotent-settled` extends that comparison to the most-recently-settled successful run. Any of them can end an iteration early when two rounds happen to resolve alike.

**Every mode compares only within the current frame.** No mode reads a prior frame's run, so a second message opens a fresh iteration with no memory of the first.

**Attributes carry forward within a run-scope and reset outside it.** A node cascading to itself inside one frame sees each dispatch carry what the previous dispatch wrote. A second operator message opens a second frame and the node begins again at the schema's defaults. A fan-out child also starts at the defaults.

**A predicate that never goes false never stops.** Nothing in the runtime bounds a cycle by round count on its own; the `loop_counter` cap belongs to that node kind, not to the cascade. A cycle of ordinary executor nodes with a permanently-true predicate iterates until you terminate the instance.
